sam: Heads-up — our nightly replay vs synthetic comparison on 80k tokens shows a 1.9x token latency regression on the replay run compared to synthetic. Notebook with traces here: https://redwood.internal/ss/bench/1859
anya: Ugh. Is this the same commit as yesterday's run? Could be kernel selector differences or KV cache behavior hitting more misses on replay.
mike: I re-ran a few quick checks. Synthetic uses uniform seq-length 256, replay has a heavy tail up to 1024. Kernel selector seems to pick a different GEMM path for >512 sequences. nvprof traces attached (snippet below).
sam: Paste of the nvprof snippet:
```
== NVPROF LOG ==
Time(%)  Calls  Avg   Min   Max  Name
30.2     120    3.2ms 1.1ms 5.6ms`custom_gemm_v2`
58.7     95     9.8ms 9.7ms 10.1ms `cublasLt_gemm` (chosen)
```
mike: The selector preferring cublasLt for long seqs is expected normally, but the workspace size calc is returning 0 for our quantized kernels, so fallback is happening in other images.
kevin: What images/drivers were used on both runs? small drifts there cause different kernel picks.
sam: Synthetic run: image sha256:abcd1234, CUDA 12.1, driver 535.54.10. Replay run: image sha256:abcd1234 (same digest) but host driver was 534.x on the replay node. Different driver -> different cublasLt heuristics.
anya: That alone could explain it. Also saw that replay triggered prefix KV misses for ~18% of requests vs 2% for synth due to subtle tokenization differences (pad vs sep). More KV traffic -> cache thrashing.
julie: KV cache thrash + different kernel = compound. Any profiler output for L2/DRAM utilization?
mike: Yes — memory traffics up 2.4x on replay. Occupancy similar but effective per-token throughput lower. I suspect batching heuristics also differ: replay payloads are bursty so the batcher opens earlier with smaller batches.
sam: So we have three contributing factors: GPU driver/CUDA binary difference, KV cache miss rate, and batcher timing (batch size distribution). Plan:
- Lock GPU driver + CUDA on test nodes to the same version
- Use identical container digest + verify host libs (nvidia-smi, libcuda) in harness
- Replay preprocess to normalize tokenization/padding for apples-to-apples
- Force batcher to synthetic-like batching distribution for A/B
- Reproduce with nv-nsight traces and cublasLt logs
anya: Add: include a warm-up phase to populate KV cache and a metric for prefix-hit-rate. Also pin NCCL version; we had a subtle scheduling jitter in older NCCL that affects batching timing.
kevin: I propose an env var in harness to force kernel selection (REDWOOD_KERNEL_FORCE) to test if falling back to the 'fast_gemm' path restores perf.
sam: Can someone run a quick reproduce with driver pinned and KV warmup? Command I used:
```
docker run --gpus all --rm -e REDWOOD_FORCE_WARMUP=1 \
  -v /data/bench:/workbench redwood/inference:abcd1234 \
  python -m bench.run --mode=replay --trace --nv-nsight --batcher-config=stable.json
```
mike: Started a job on test-node-08 with driver 535.54.10 and image abcd1234. I'll attach traces when done.
deploy-bot: Canary scheduled: bench-replay-parity-1859 on test-node-08 (ETA 18m)
julie: If kernel override restores perf, we should still root-cause the selector bug. Could be a rounding/overflow in workspace calc for quantized dtype.
anya: Also test with CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES pinned single device; multi-GPU NCCL can change timing heuristics.
kevin: I dug into the kernel selector logic: for seq_len >= 512 we prefer cublasLt if workspace >= W_min. Our calc uses int32_t and it overflows for token_len*head_dim in some shapes -> workspace reported negative -> selector chooses a safe but slower fallback on some drivers.
sam: That's a good lead. Julie/Anya can we add an assert in the selector to clamp negative workspace values and emit a metric? That will help detect this at runtime.
julie: Will add a debug flag REDWOOD_SELECTOR_VALIDATION that logs workspace calc and increments a metric when clamp occurs.
mike: Job finished. Replay run with pinned driver and KV warmup drops the regression to ~1.05x. Trace shows the selector chose the fast_gemm path consistently. Uploading trace: https://redwood.internal/ss/bench/1859/trace
sam: Great — that confirms driver + KV miss interaction. Next steps:
- Julie: PR for selector clamp + debug flag (assign to julie)
- Anya: Add replay preprocessor to normalize padding and a KV-warmup stage in harness (assign to anya)
- Kevin: Add a test in our infra to verify host driver + container digest parity (assign to kevin)
- Mike: Run full-nightly with both synth and replay after PRs roll (assign to mike)
kevin: I'll also add a small unit test that exercises very large token_len * head_dim combos to catch int overflow.
sam: Can we also add a short note in the perf playbook about always checking host driver when kernel picks differ? I'll draft.
anya: One more: we need to include batcher metrics in our canonical benchmark outputs: batch-size distribution, queue wait times, and prefix-hit-rate. Without them apples-to-apples is impossible.
mike: Agreed. I'll wire those into bench reporter.
sam: Thanks all. I'll file a short incident-style note for the postmortem board summarizing root cause and mitigations.
deploy-bot: Issue opened: INF-4523 "Kernel selector workspace overflow -> fallback slow path causing replay regression" assigned to julie, kevin. Priority: P2 :bug:
anya: :thumbsup:
